title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

reading.body:
Instinct is an AI assistant for task management that collects personal information to train its models by default, requiring users to actively opt out through settings or use a protected vault. Even when users disconnect connected accounts like Gmail, the system retains indexed data and can continue accessing stored information. The assistant can also make autonomous purchases using shared payment methods, with disputes over unintended transactions falling to the user and merchant rather than to Instinct itself.

The deployment shows a failure to make data use transparent and to require affirmative consent before training on personal information. What would have caught this: making data privacy the default rather than requiring users to discover and navigate opt-out settings, deleting indexed data when accounts are disconnected, requiring explicit user confirmation before any autonomous action including purchases, and assigning liability to the system provider rather than shifting it to users.

It is not established whether Instinct's design choices were intentional, whether users suffered actual financial or privacy harm, or what proportion of users discovered the opt-out mechanisms.

reports.title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

summary:
Instinct is a new artificial intelligence assistant that helps organize daily tasks, but it presents significant privacy and security risks. By default, Instinct uses personal information to train its AI models unless users actively opt out through settings or use a protected vault feature. Additionally, even after disconnecting connected accounts like Gmail, Instinct retains indexed data and can continue accessing stored information. The assistant can also make purchases on your behalf using shared payment methods, and disputes over unintended purchases fall between you and the merchant rather than Instinct.

Norton offers an alternative approach with its Family Assistant, which keeps user data private and does not use shared information to train AI models. Unlike Instinct, Norton Family Assistant requires explicit user confirmation before taking actions such as submitting forms or booking appointments. Users can easily delete any data shared with Norton by deleting their account or removing specific instances within the assistant settings. The article emphasizes that consumers should not sacrifice personal data security to benefit from AI assistant technology.
